lines.text: In South Africa, there's an account where your savings grow completely tax-free.
But many people never open one.
It's called a Tax-Free Savings Account.
Each tax year, you can put in up to R46 000.
If you don't use it, you lose it. Unused space doesn't carry over.
Over your whole life, you can put in up to R500 000.
The interest, dividends and growth you earn are never taxed.
And that growth doesn't count towards your limits. So your account can grow way past R500 000.
But watch out for two traps.
One: Put in more than the limit, and SARS charges a 40% penalty on the extra.
Two: Money you take out can't be put back for free. Putting it back counts as a new contribution.
So treat it as long-term money. Open one at your bank or an investment app. Start small, and start early.
Follow Money From Zero for more money tips, made simple.
